findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body: When cleanup is called while the socket remains active, the `message` handler remains registered and continues receiving events. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles can retain stale handlers, duplicate processing, and increase memory usage. Restore the call to `socket.off("message", handler)`.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. If the socket remains active after cleanup, later messages still invoke stale handlers; repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate listeners and duplicate processing.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup callback
findings.body:
Any caller invoking the returned disposer expects the registered `"message"` handler to be detached. With a socket that emits afterward, the handler still runs; repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate listeners, causing duplicate processing and memory retention.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal when disposing the attachment
findings.body:
The returned disposer no longer unregisters the handler. After a session closes or authorization is revoked, subsequent attacker-controlled `"message"` events still reach the stale handler, crossing the intended lifecycle/trust boundary. Repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate listeners, enabling message-driven resource exhaustion.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Detach the message listener in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
When cleanup is called while the socket remains alive, the handler stays registered and retains its captured state. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate listeners, causing duplicate message processing, memory growth, and eventual listener-limit warnings.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
